description: The NRC Reactor Operating Experience Analysis and Trend Summary, 2022 update, is an Idaho National Laboratory report (INL/RPT-24-77217, March 2024) by Zhegang Ma for the NRC Division of Risk Assessment, summarising reactor operating experience analyses with data through 2022. It brings together the reliability and frequency trends identified in the 2022 update reports for the component performance study, the loss of offsite power analysis, the initiating events analysis and the system study, which are published on the NRC Reactor Operating Experience Results and Databases website. Chapters cover loss of offsite power events, rates of initiating events, component performance studies for air-operated valves, emergency diesel generators, motor-driven pumps, motor-operated valves and turbine-driven pumps with increasing and decreasing trends, and system performance studies such as auxiliary feedwater, emergency power and high-pressure coolant injection. Coverage is the U.S. commercial reactor fleet. Access: a PDF on the INL site, free, with a warranty disclaimer and no licence text. Caveats: summary trends, with detailed data in the linked database site. It suits reliability inputs for nuclear probabilistic risk and resilience models, and relates to the NRC datasets on US nuclear facilities catalogued here.
